short: Cornish engineer who built the first full-scale working railway steam locomotive.
full:
Richard Trevithick was a pioneering inventor in the mining industry of Cornwall, where he recognised the potential of "strong steam" — high-pressure steam engines that were significantly smaller and more powerful than James Watt's low-pressure designs. In 1801, he successfully demonstrated the "Puffing Devil", one of the first steam-powered road vehicles, though it famously caught fire days later.

His most historically significant achievement came in 1804 at the Penydarren Ironworks in Wales, where he built the world's first steam railway locomotive to successfully haul a load along rails. Despite his brilliance, Trevithick lacked business acumen and repeatedly fell into financial ruin, dying in poverty while his high-pressure innovations laid the groundwork for the global railway revolution.
